central_topic: Choosing a small subset of k benchmarks to run on a new model and imputing its scores on the remaining benchmarks from a historical model-by-benchmark score matrix (MTEB, HELM Lite, Open LLM Leaderboard); post-draft gaps concern benchmark-level comparator literature, the benchmark-redundancy premise, and sources for the Open LLM Leaderboard and its component benchmarks.
core_methods: EM-fitted Gaussian with missing data and conditional-mean imputation
comparators: prediction of unrun benchmark scores from a few observed benchmarks
low-rank or matrix-completion imputation of LLM model-by-benchmark score matrices
adaptive or IRT-based active selection for LLM evaluation
benchmarks: Open LLM Leaderboard (IFEval, BBH, MATH Level 5, GPQA, MuSR, MMLU-Pro)
result_driven_themes: redundancy and low-dimensional structure among LLM benchmark scores

queries.query: predicting language model performance on unseen benchmarks from scores on a subset of benchmarks
queries.rationale: Related Work claims novelty ('the unit of selection is a whole benchmark and the target is every benchmark not run') but cites only item-level work; the closest competitors predict unrun benchmark scores from a few observed ones. Targets gap related-work-comparators.

queries.query: matrix completion low-rank factorization of model-by-benchmark score matrix for LLM evaluation
queries.rationale: Related Work calls matrix completion 'the standard alternatives for filling score matrices' but cites only generic sources (Candes, Salakhutdinov); need work applying it to LLM score matrices. Targets gap related-work-comparators.

queries.query: adaptive testing item response theory active selection of evaluations for large language models
queries.rationale: Adaptive or IRT-based selection of what to run is the third competing direction named in the gap memo; existing bibliography has only Embretson (textbook), Vania (test-set comparison), and item-reduction papers. Targets gap related-work-comparators.

queries.query: redundancy and correlation among LLM benchmarks low-dimensional structure of benchmark scores
queries.rationale: Introduction says benchmark suites 'are known to overlap in what they measure' but cites only the suites themselves; need empirical evidence of benchmark redundancy. BenchBench and Observational Scaling Laws are already cited, so the query is aimed at redundancy/correlation analyses beyond those. Targets gap intro-benchmark-redundancy-claim.

queries.query: Open LLM Leaderboard v2 evaluation of open language models
queries.rationale: The Open LLM Leaderboard is one of three sealed evaluation datasets (3371 history and 300 held-out models) and has no citation, while HELM and MTEB do. Targets gap data-open-llm-leaderboard-context.

queries.query: IFEval instruction-following, BIG-Bench Hard, GPQA, MuSR, MMLU-Pro benchmark
queries.rationale: The six leaderboard component benchmarks (IFEval, BBH, MATH Level 5, GPQA, MuSR, MMLU-Pro) are named in the protocol and appendix without citations. Targets gap data-open-llm-leaderboard-context.

forbidden_query_patterns: chronology of campaign cycles, ideas, or attempts
internal terms such as combined_score, rubric, program_1, eligible
queries naming or hinting at the prior published paper on this exact task (do not search for its title, authors, or results)
re-searching already-cited directions: tinyBenchmarks, metabench, anchor points, Sloth, observational scaling laws, BenchBench, EM, stacking, submodular selection, ridge, MTEB, HELM, MMLU, BIG-bench
